steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...This is my report on the Far North Incident. I will submit my written report within one week.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Thank you, Lieutenant. But I still have questions.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: What you've mentioned—getting into the mining district, investigating the miners, evacuating them under the Armies' gunfire... those are merely the process.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: An event must have cause, process, and result, just like how crops grow from seeds, and yield fruits.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I apologize for my poor presentation, Your High Excellency, but I have mentioned both the cause of the event and how we handled the aftermath.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: All scattered information. You have described the details, but you have not seen the big picture. How can the reader understand what the writer fails to perceive?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Have you forgotten how to write a report in the five years since you graduated from the military academy? Or do you want me to submit a fragmented, incomplete report to His Imperial Majesty?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I can forgive your youthful errors, but Ursus cannot afford to wait.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I apologize. I will fill in the gaps in the written report—

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: We do not have the time to address the consequences of your omissions. The price of trial and error is too high.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I need you to tell me, right here, right now. What role do you think Grand Duchess Elisabeth played? Were there signs of her association with the Armies? As for the Infected that we rescued...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Can they truly be of help to us?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I'm not sure I have sufficient information to talk about it in an informed manner...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You experienced the events first-hand. No one is more informed than you.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Speak, child. I will listen.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...I believe that the Grand Duchess was simply going with the flow.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: She had learned about the Royal Guard's death and the miners' escape before we even planned to enter the mining district.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: All she needed to do was to let a little information out, and the Fourth Army would have an excuse to 'clean up', and proceed towards the Central Governorate under the pretext of quelling the rebellion.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: This way, the Grand Duchess could cover up the death of a Royal Guard on her watch, and the Army can deploy on the borders of the Central Governorate... as it does now.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: As for why the Army is doing this... I believe you know better than anyone.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: They mistake the Tsar's benevolence for weakness. They will pay the price.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: I concur with most of your speculation, Elotta. But there is one thing you are missing—the Yurodstvo.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It disappeared. I could not confirm whether it was real or not, and I do not even feel the need to dig any deeper. After all... we witnessed the burning of the last Yurodstvo with our own eyes.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You do not believe it was the Yurodstvo who appeared in the Far North?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I simply believe you know more than I do.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: The troubling madman... a poisonous relic of an older era. I will get to the bottom of it. Ursus does not need a Yurodstvo anymore.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Now, let us get back to the topic at hand. Were their goals accomplished, Lieutenant?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: They failed to hush up news of the ore vein exhaustion. Which leads us to your other question—

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Can the Infected that we rescued truly be of help to us? In fact, they've already helped.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The belt of torches on the ice awakened all the outposts around Lake Neva on the Grypherburg side. Every household in Ursus has heard their message.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: 'Ursus abandoned them! Who will be next?' Everyone asks the same question: the newspapers, intercity comms, late-night radio...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The miners in the mines ask, the workers in the city ask; wealthy citizens ask, poor vagabonds ask; soldiers ask, students ask.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The Grand Duchess expected the miners to die in the Far North. But they survived, testifying to the exhaustion of the ore veins, and exposing the inadequacy of the reforms—

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Slow, gradual improvement is not enough for the pressing needs of Ursus's development.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: We must act, before even more people are fed into the hungry machine of the Empire.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You said yourself that Ursus can no longer afford to wait...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You're digressing, Lieutenant.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: You said Rhodes Island helped the Infected miners send the message.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Yes. Right now, however, we should focus on—

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: What do you think of Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...We should be vigilant.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: They demonstrated military-level coordination during the tracking and evacuation process, and they possess a natural advantage in their understanding of the Infected. There are plenty of reasons to be vigilant.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Or perhaps, their strength is something that we can leverage.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: As far as I am aware, Rhodes Island has no permanent presence in Ursus. Perhaps we can invite them to set up a branch office in Grypherburg or a nearby city...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The Grand Duchess might strike first.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: She's not one to be rash. Did you mention the name 'Kal'tsit' to the Rhodes Islanders?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Yes. They said that Kal'tsit previously served as a physician at Rhodes Island, but had died in an accident.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Are you certain?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I've dispatched a unit to the scene of the incident to ascertain. From what we know so far, there is no reason to think otherwise.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: So... Kal'tsit is dead.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: The name that Chairman Witte extracted from the Chernobog lab files is no longer of use.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Because of the Sarcophagus, of course. Ursus needs its energy.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I don't know the specifics, unfortunately.

options: But Witte gave you a name: Kal'tsit.
He wanted you to find Kal'tsit through us.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Of course. Otherwise, he wouldn't have sent me alone—

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...Sent me to the Far North alone.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Yes, he trusts me. It's the duty of a soldier to follow orders, and it's not my place to complain, even if I should die in the Far North.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: But it shouldn't be this way. Miners and civilians were massacred, but the Grand Duchess gets out unscathed, and the Army is able to deploy a stone's throw from Grypherburg with no consequences.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: This isn't how things should be! How can I go back like this...?

options: If I told you, there was a way to bring Kal'tsit back to life...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Are you joking? How is that possible? Is this Kal'tsit like the fae of legend, able to return to life whenever she wants?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Wait a moment. The Chairman did say that the secret police once believed Director Kal'tsit to have died in that incident...

spans.text: Wait a moment. The Chairman did say that the secret police
believed Director Kal'tsit to have died in that incident...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You just tell me like that? Did you think I would trust you the same way in return? You're not even Ursine—

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: What if some of us used to be?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Even if you really do know nothing, we won't forget that you once stood with us there, helping evacuate the Infected.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: We appreciate what you did, Lieutenant Gorchekova, even if you don't need our thanks. Am I right?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Tell me, and I'll listen, once again as a child of Ursus.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Alright, I knew I couldn't resist the chance to awaken a straying Ursine's identity.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: What I know about the Sarcophagus is very limited...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: —Lieutenant?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I'm sorry. I think I got distracted.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: It's alright. Bad habits of the elderly. I can't stop myself when I start talking about the motherland and our future with the youth...

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Perhaps you really do need rest. I've taken up too much of your time.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: No, Your High Excellency, I was simply thinking about what you said—

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Get some rest, Lieutenant.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Unlike the Far North, Grypherburg still sees some daylight this time of year. Do not forget to finish your report, once you've rested.

a.text: 'As the mines begin to reopen gradually in the Northern Tundra, the Third Army casts its gaze towards the Central Governorate.'
'The Fourth Army continues its illegal presence on the border of the Central Governorate. All citizens are advised to respect the cordon and refrain from traveling to the Lake Neva area.'

'The First Army has begun to conscript students from dozens of universities in the Central Governorate, without authorization from the State Council. Student protests across the country are being bloodily suppressed.'
'The Second and Seventh Armies have been mobilized, in response to Grypherburg's request...'

steps.name: Student A
steps.text: That's all you see in the papers these days. I've got a cousin going to school in the Central Governorate. Haven't heard from her in a while.

steps.name: Student B
steps.text: Did you hear? Uchitelnitsa Koshelna didn't go to Deity Grypherburg Imperial University. She went to the mines to teach the miners how to read!

steps.name: Student B
steps.text: That's so brave and selfless of her. I want to follow in her footsteps when I graduate...

steps.name: Student B
steps.text: I hope we'll see her again.

steps.name: Student C
steps.text: Don't listen to everything you read in the papers! It's all bad news to make us anxious and demoralize us.

steps.name: Student C
steps.text: The student council is holding a protest in Igor Memorial Park. Are you going?

steps.name: Student B
steps.text: Of course!

steps.name: Student A
steps.text: M-Me too!

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: There's a lot of movement in the military. Student and worker strikes are taking place all across the country, but they're being suppressed even swifter and more harshly than before...

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Also, the Grypherburg police recently arrested a student from the Literature Department attempting to graffiti the grand hall of the State Council. I heard the Petrachevsky Group is soliciting donations and trying to get him released.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: It's true, I checked with them. Every underground tabloid is spreading the news about him, and the words he wrote on the walls of the council hall.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: The underground tabloids are printing far quicker than the censors can keep up.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Let's put that in the next letter to Sonya.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: They should be on their way back to Grypherburg, come to think of it...

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Write anyway. There are curfews everywhere. There's no guarantee they'll make it back on schedule.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Yes... I hope things go smoothly on their side.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: They will.

steps.name: Worker?
steps.text: Getting in wasn't that hard.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Just because I hacked the monitors doesn't mean you can let your guard down. They say the session has been suspended indefinitely, but they could also resume at any time.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: The corridor leading to the meeting hall is still being patrolled four times an hour. Not counting the time it takes to get out, you have eight minutes to leave your mark.

steps.name: Worker?
steps.text: Pee? Break something and take a piece?

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: ...Can you do something that doesn't make so much noise and actually means something?

steps.name: Worker?
steps.text: Well... I'll think about it.

steps.name: Worker?
steps.text: Why do I have to dress like this, anyway? It's not like my normal clothes are all that conspicuous.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: You're wearing a Grypherburg plumber's uniform. They don't have a seat on the council, but they have access to the council hall, and they're responsible for maintenance work throughout the building.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: While there's no way for students like us—complete non-producers—to gain access to the council, much less gain any real influence.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Bah, why am I even explaining all this to you? I'm hanging up. You have six minutes.

steps.name: Voice in Earpiece
steps.text: Botani out.

steps.name: Worker?
steps.text: Lokh.

steps.name: Worker?
steps.text: What should I do? Six minutes...
The student in the plumber's uniform casts his gaze towards the end of the council hall, where the symbol of Ursine divine glory shines bright on the wall.
He thinks for a moment, then squints and pulls out a can of red spraypaint.
Brekin is not on duty today, but his colleague, who lives next door to him, sent his youngest son to his place and asked him to take his shift today, because he had a fever and a splitting headache.
Brekin, being the kind-hearted man he is, agreed. Scarcely could he imagine what he would see when he walked into the council hall—

steps.name: Cleaner
steps.text: Gosudar-batyushka—
The golden symbol on the wall is fully covered in red paint. Beneath it are words written with the same red paint, in the Ursine language—

a.text: <color=#FF4200>'The victor displays the emblem of the vanquished for his vanity, but he will forever stand in the shadow of the vanquished, if he cannot cast it away.'</color>
<color=#FF4200>—Yakov Petrov, penned in prison in the autumn of 1076</color>
